why: Both analyses land on essentially the same hedgehog (cost-lowering hospital products: IV, nutrition, diagnostics), the same stop-doing items (exit consumer brands, quit the blockbuster race) and the same brutal facts, with profit per employee only as a secondary denominator in each. Analysis 2 is more explicit about confidence and uncomfortable truths, but Analysis 1 backs diagnostics and the hospital core more decisively and reads the company's potential closer to the key, so it is marginally the better one to hand to the leader.
